This game got so hard, I was shaking during the boss battle:

+Meaningful progression, game feels like an adventure despite being a handful of generated maps.
+Enough Characters / Items / Ways to play to keep the game refreshing.
+Soundtrack is dope, and so are the sound effects
+Gameplay is smooth
+Character design is top, something for every playstyle
+Multiplayer works well

+/- Very tough, like, VERY.

-Only downside is really that I found there was only a handful of level bosses, so you'll end up fighting the same ones over and over. Not much of a downside, because you can develop playstyles around them, but does take away from the freshness of each playthrough slightly

Overall, very fun, but also challenging platform / roguelite game, with enough elements to keep the game fresh for many playthroughs.
Great soundtrack. Great way to kill an hour. 6/10

Risk of Rain is a frustrating slog about beating down crowds of enemies that stand directly against of the game's supposed incentive structure.

The game sells time = difficulty, but this equation doesn't involve the consideration of the player for the majority of any given run as every enemy must be killed to leave an area (near the end of the game, [spoiler]the player may choose to go to another level or the end-game, but the end-game isn't super hard, so the decision is largely one of spectacle in the case that a crazy-looking load of items has dropped[/spoiler]). Most of the game is walking back and forth with a pea-shooter, unloading your attacks into bullet-sponge enemies for minutes at a time.

the success of your run depends largely on the random items generated--especially early in the game because bad drops in the first level leave you incapable of killing enemies while the difficulty rises (because time = difficulty) to no fault of yours (since you can't focus down a boss to abandon a stage).

Unlockable characters provide meaningful variety since they aren't balanced at all. One can block all damage happening one one side of him while dealing large area-of-effect damage, which largely trivializes the game since it's about downing swarms of enemies with far too much health. Another character has a particular high damage attack that if it kills its target has its cooldown refunded, but since you can't aim the attack in a two-dimensional space, the attack is completely moot.

The game looks and sounds nice, which is mostly a waste as retrying the game until you get a salvageable set of equipment only allows you to spend frustrating, agonizing minutes ineffectually chipping down enemy life bars.
